title: Spencer Tillman: From OU Captain to College Football Broadcaster
question: Which former OU running back became a CBS and Fox college football analyst?
answer: Spencer Tillman, an OU running back from 1983 to 1986, became a broadcaster and was CBS's lead college football studio analyst from 1999 to 2014 before joining Fox Sports.
summary: Spencer Tillman, a captain on OU's 1985 title team, became a TV sportscaster and spent 16 years as CBS's lead college football studio analyst, then joined Fox.
body: Spencer Tillman, a Tulsa Edison product, played running back at Oklahoma from 1983 to 1986. He burst onto the scene as the Big Eight Newcomer of the Year in 1983 and later captained the 1985 Sooners, who beat Penn State 25-10 in the Orange Bowl to win the national championship. He was named MVP of the Orange Bowl played in January 1987 and entered the Orange Bowl Hall of Fame in 2012.

Tillman spent eight seasons in the NFL with the Houston Oilers and San Francisco 49ers. In San Francisco he was part of the team that won Super Bowl XXIV and served as a co-captain alongside Joe Montana and Ronnie Lott.

He started preparing for life after football while still playing, working as an anchor and reporter at KPRC-TV in Houston during the offseason. That led to a long run as a KPRC sports anchor and then weekend sports anchor duties at WABC-TV in New York from 1997 to 1999.

His big national break came in 1999, when CBS Sports made him the lead studio analyst for College Football Today. He held that seat for 16 years, through 2014, and from 2000 to 2003 he also called regional NFL games with Tim Brando. In 2015 he joined Fox Sports as a college football game analyst, reuniting with Brando.
Tillman also wrote a leadership book, Scoring in the Red Zone, and completed an executive education program at Harvard Business School, proof that the captain's armband suited him off the field too.
